title: Seat the removable winch handle on the drive hub
instruction: Put the handle on the winch.
context: Boat-trailer and utility winches (Dutton-Lainson, Fulton and similar) use a removable hand crank that has to be seated on a square drive before the drum can be wound or paid out. A handle left off, or only hooked on the shaft, will slip when a load comes on. Dutton-Lainson sells the 6454 9-3/8 in removable handle as the official crank for the DLB1500A (drawing DD_DLB1500A, TUFFPLATE sku 14964). This trial is only that seating step: pick the handle from a marked outline beside the winch, align its hub with the drive shaft, slide it on to the spring-pin depth, and let go. The drum is not wound. The trial is unpowered.
setup: A compact Dutton-Lainson DLB1500A-class trailer winch (zinc TUFFPLATE body, dark 2 in strap on the drum, side plates, gear on the brake side, fairlead and hook, slotted base) sits in the middle of the table, unpowered, with its square drive pointing toward the left arm. The official 9-3/8 in removable handle, with a black molded grip, starts on a marked outline beside the hub, parallel to the shaft but not on its axis. All props are rigid and start on fixed marks. The colliding envelope is compact versus the real 7-7/32 in x 5-1/2 in unit so the grip stays in reach; that scale is stated in Fidelity.
scoring: As seen in the overhead video, the handle stays on the drive shaft. At the end, after 1 s at rest and with the gripper 3 cm clear of the handle: 1.0 once the hub is on the shaft to the pin depth, aligned, and has been let go; 0.5 if the hub has at least 10 mm of engagement but is short of the pin depth, or if it is fully seated but has not been let go or is not yet still; 0 if the handle is still on its outline, misses the shaft, or is only pressed along a pre-aligned start. The handle starts beside the shaft, not already on it. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Handle starts beside the shaft on its marked outline, not on it. The drum is not wound.
fidelity: The winch and handle are rigid bodies at recognisable DLB1500A proportions. Tight square-on-square is not representable at a 4 mm PhysX contactOffset, so the shaft is scored geometrically on a looser 14 mm peg in a 40 mm hub with a 12 mm axial seat window (flagged). The colliding envelope is compact versus the real 7-7/32 in x 5-1/2 in unit so the grip stays in reach (flagged). The drum is not wound. The spring pin is scored as a depth, not a simulated detent.
scores: Scripted (yam_arena, 320x176, seed 0; Brev L40S, v1g): demo 1.0 (step 265); short 0.5; idle 0.0; naive 0.0. Dream-1 flash (seed 1, 22 Nov 2026): 0.0 in 700 steps, not refused (handle nudged on the bench, never seated).
